greek.forms: Singular: πόλεμος, πολέμου, πολέμῳ, πόλεμον; Plural: πόλεμοι, πολέμων, πολέμοις, πολέμους
greek.etymology: From PIE *pel- (to strike, clash). English descendants: Polemic (controversial argument), Polemical (aggressively controversial), Polemicist (one who argues controversially), Polemics (art of controversial debate)
greek.literary_context: Herodotus, Histories 1.87, written during the 5th century BCE, chronicling the Persian Wars
greek.usage_example: ἐν πολέμῳ γὰρ οὐ τὰ αὐτὰ συμφέρει — For in war the same things are not advantageous
greek.did_you_know: Ancient Greeks had a god specifically for the panic and fear felt in battle - Phobos, son of Ares. His name literally meant "flight" and gave us our word "phobia." He rode into πόλεμος alongside his brother Deimos (Dread).
